annotations.title: Find Entity by MAC or Name

description:
Search for any Mist entity across all entity types with a single query. Pass a MAC address (any notation: aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, AA-BB-CC-DD-EE-FF), an IPv4 address (e.g. 10.0.0.1), or a hostname/name string and the tool fans out across wireless clients, wired clients, WAN clients, NAC clients, devices (inventory), Mist Edge appliances, guests, and user MAC assignments in parallel. Results are normalized to a common shape: entity_type, id, mac, name, site_id, site_name. MAC queries use OUI prefix matching to prioritize the most likely entity type first (e.g. 02:00:00 OUI → Mist Edge searched first; Juniper AP OUIs → device searched first). IP queries fan out in parallel across wireless, wired, and WAN clients. NAME SEARCH — PREFIX MATCHING: the Mist API performs prefix matching on hostname/name queries. A query of 'everest' is automatically sent as 'everest*' so it will match 'everest-4', 'everest-ap1', etc. You do NOT need to add a wildcard yourself — pass the plain prefix (e.g. 'everest', not 'everest*'). Use entity_types to restrict the search when you already know the entity category. Partial failures (individual entity type search errors) are reported in summary.errors and do not prevent results from other types being returned. Follow up with search_mist_data for paginated searches within a specific type, or get_mist_config to retrieve the full configuration record for a found entity.

Searchable entity types:
- wireless_client: Wireless clients currently associated over WiFi (search_type: wireless_clients)
- wired_client: Clients connected through managed switches (search_type: wired_clients)
- wan_client: Clients connected through WAN gateways (search_type: wan_clients)
- nac_client: NAC (802.1X/RADIUS) authenticated clients (search_type: nac_clients)
- device: Network devices in org inventory (APs, switches, gateways, routers) (search_type: inventory)
- mxedge: Mist Edge appliances (search_type: mxedges)
- guest: Guest portal authorization entries (search_type: guest_authorizations)
- usermac: User-to-MAC address assignments (PSK/NAC user mappings) (search_type: usermacs)

duration.description: Time range duration (e.g. '1d', '1h', '10m'). Alternative to start_time/end_time. Applied only to entity types that support time range filtering.

end_time.description: End of time range — epoch timestamp in seconds or relative string (e.g. 'now', '-1h'). Applied only to entity types that support time range filtering.

entity_types.description: Optional list of entity types to search. When omitted all registered entity types are searched.

limit.description: Maximum results to return per entity type (default: 100, max: 1000).

org_id.description: Organization UUID to search within (required). Use get_mist_self to discover available org IDs.

query.description: The search string: a MAC address (any notation), an IPv4 address, or a hostname/name prefix (pass the plain prefix — the wildcard suffix is added automatically). See the tool description for how each format is matched.

site_id.description: Optional site UUID to narrow results to a specific site. Use get_mist_config(resource_type='sites') to discover site IDs.

start_time.description: Start of time range — epoch timestamp in seconds or relative string (e.g. '-1d', '-1w', '-2h'). Applied only to entity types that support time range filtering.

name: find_mist_entity
title: Find Entity by MAC or Name

description:
Read any Mist configuration object by type. Supports org-scope and site-scope. Provide org_id always. If site_id is also provided, the request is scoped to that site where the type supports it. Omit resource_id to list all objects of that type; provide resource_id to get a single object. Pagination: a conservative default page size is applied per resource type; if a response has has_more=true, call again with its next_cursor.

Available resource types:
- sites: Sites within the organization. Use to discover site_ids for site-scoped operations. [org]
- alarmtemplates: Alarm rule templates for sites or org [org]
- deviceprofiles: Device configuration profiles [org]
- gatewaytemplates: Gateway templates for site gateways (SRX/SSR) [org]
- networktemplates: Switch network configuration templates [org]
- networks: Network subnets and user segments [org]
- rftemplates: Radio frequency templates for AP radio settings [org]
- services: Application definitions for security policies [org]
- servicepolicies: Security and firewall policies [org]
- sitegroups: Groups of sites for bulk configuration [org]
- sitetemplates: Site attribute templates [org]
- vpns: WAN overlay VPN configurations [org]
- webhooks: Real-time event push webhook configurations [org+site]
- wlantemplates: WLAN, tunneling, and WxLAN policy collections [org]
- wlans: Wireless network (SSID) configs. Org-scope: deploy across sites via wlantemplates. Site-scope: single site only. scope=org for multi-site SSIDs; scope=site for single-site. Merged effective list: GET /sites/{site_id}/wlans/derived (not a resource_type). [org+site]
- psks: Multi pre-shared key configurations [org+site]
- wxrules: WLAN restriction rules [org+site]
- wxtags: Tags for WxRules [org+site]
- evpn_topologies: EVPN VxLAN/MP-BGP fabric configurations [org+site]
- nactags: NAC tags for building NAC rules [org]
- nacrules: NAC rules for network access control [org]
- avprofiles: Antivirus profiles for malware detection [org]
- idpprofiles: Intrusion detection and prevention profiles [org]
- aamwprofiles: Sky ATP advanced anti-malware profiles [org]
- mxclusters: Mist Edge clusters for HA and load balancing [org]
- mxedges: Mist Edge appliances [org+site]
- mxtunnels: Mist tunnels for VLAN tunneling [org]
- devices: Device config records (APs, switches, gateways). Only returns devices with a site-level config record — org template-managed devices will not appear. Config read/write only. Use get_mist_stats(stats_type='site_devices') for device inventory. [org+site]
- maps: Site floor plan maps [site only]

limit.description: Maximum items per page. A conservative per-type default applies and a hard ceiling is enforced per type (higher values are clamped). Pass an explicit value to override for this call.

next_cursor.description: Cursor from a prior response's next_cursor. When provided, all other pagination parameters (limit, page) are ignored.

org_id.description: Organization UUID. Use get_mist_self to discover available org IDs.

page.description: Page number for offset-based pagination (1-based, default: 1).

resource_id.description: Specific resource UUID to retrieve. Omit to list all resources of this type.

resource_type.description: Type of configuration object to retrieve

site_id.description: Site UUID (optional). When provided, the request is scoped to this site if the resource type supports it. Use get_mist_config(resource_type='sites') to discover site IDs.

name: get_mist_constants
title: Get Platform Constants

description:
Retrieve AI-powered analytics, troubleshooting, and performance metrics from the Mist Cloud. Each insight_type (marvis_actions, troubleshoot, insight_metrics, sle) targets a different analytical capability — see the list below for scope and required params.

Type-specific parameters go in the 'params' object. Time range: use start_time/end_time (epoch seconds or relative like '-1d') or duration (e.g. '1d'). Pagination: pass next_cursor from a prior response, or use page + limit.

Available insight types:
[Marvis]
  - marvis_actions: AI-powered network suggestions from Marvis. Includes Marvis Minis-detected connectivity failures (DHCP, ARP, DNS, app reachability). Prioritized issues across connectivity, infrastructure, wireless, wired, AP, switch, and gateway. Use to answer 'what's wrong with the network?' [org_id required] [no time-range] (labs/preview) | params: active, category, priority, status, symptom
[Troubleshoot]
  - troubleshoot: Marvis AI troubleshooting for sites, devices, and clients. Max 7 days. Requires Marvis license. site_id or params.mac required (400 if both omitted). start_time max 7 days ago. [org_id required] [time-range] requires Marvis subscription | params: mac, type
[Metrics]
  - insight_metrics: Site-level performance metrics by object_type (site, client, ap, gateway, mxedge, switch) and metric name. Call get_mist_constants with constant_type='insight_metrics' for valid metric names. Provide mac for client/ap/mxedge/switch/gateway. For gateway traffic use metric=bytes, rx_bytes, or tx_bytes. [site_id required] [time-range] | params: interval, mac, metric*, object_type*
  - sle: SLE analytics. Org: sites_sle, org_metric. Site: summary, impact_summary, summary_trend, histogram, threshold, impacted_[applications/aps/gateways/interfaces/switches/wired_clients/wireless_clients/chassis], classifier_details, classifier_summary_trend, metrics, classifiers. Site-level: call with query_type='metrics' first to discover available SLE metrics (returns supported/enabled list for the site, e.g. coverage, capacity, time-to-connect). Org: org_id + query_type. Site: site_id + query_type + scope + scope_id + metric (except query_type=metrics or classifiers). For org_metric, metric names come from get_mist_constants(insight_metrics). [time-range] | params: classifier, interval, metric, query_type*, scope, scope_id, sle
Available params (type-specific — see insight type descriptions for which apply):
- active: Filter by active state: true (active) or false (resolved). Default: true
- category: Filter by category: connectivity, infrastructure, wireless, wired, ap, switch, or gateway
- priority: Filter by priority: high or low
- status: Filter by status: open, resolved, or snoozed
- symptom: Filter by symptom type. These values correspond to Marvis action categories (e.g. dns_failure, dhcp_failure, bad_cable, port_flap). Exact accepted values depend on the labs endpoint — use category filter instead if symptom results are unexpected.
- mac: MAC address of the device or client to troubleshoot (format: aabbccddeeff, no separators). For device/client analysis provide mac and omit site_id. For site-level analysis omit mac and provide site_id instead. (required when troubleshooting a specific device or client; omit for site-level analysis)
- type: Network type filter when troubleshooting a site (wan|wired|wireless)
- interval: Aggregation interval for metric data points (e.g. '1h', '1d')
- metric: Metric name (required) → get_mist_constants('insight_metrics')
- object_type: Type of object to get metrics for (required) (site|client|ap|gateway|mxedge|switch)
- classifier: Classifier name. Use query_type=classifiers to discover available classifiers for a metric. (required when query_type is classifier_details or classifier_summary_trend)
- query_type: SLE operation to perform. Org-level: sites_sle, org_metric. Site-level: summary, impact_summary, summary_trend, impacted_applications, impacted_aps, impacted_gateways, impacted_interfaces, impacted_switches, impacted_wired_clients, impacted_wireless_clients, impacted_chassis, histogram, threshold, classifier_details, classifier_summary_trend, metrics, classifiers (required)
- scope: SLE scope (required for all site-level query types) (site|ap|client|gateway|switch|mxedge)
- scope_id: Identifier for the scope target — format depends on scope value: scope=site → site UUID (e.g. '1234abcd-1234-1234-1234-1234abcd5678'); scope=ap/switch/gateway → device UUID from find_mist_entity or get_mist_config; scope=client → client MAC address in compact format (e.g. 'aabbccddeeff', no separators); scope=mxedge → mxedge MAC address in compact format (e.g. 'aabbccddeeff'). (required for all site-level query types)
- sle: SLE type filter. Applicable to org-level query types (sites_sle, org_metric). (wan|wifi|wired)

duration.description: Time range duration (e.g. '1d', '1h', '10m'). Alternative to start_time/end_time. Supported by troubleshoot and insight_metrics. NOTE: for troubleshoot, duration must not exceed '7d'.

end_time.description: End of time range — epoch timestamp in seconds or relative string (e.g. 'now', '-1h'). Supported by troubleshoot and insight_metrics. NOTE: for troubleshoot, the total range (start_time to end_time) must not exceed 7 days.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a prior response's next_cursor field for cursor-based pagination. When provided, other pagination params are ignored.

org_id.description: Organization UUID (required for marvis_actions and troubleshoot). Use get_mist_self to discover available org IDs.

page.description: Page number for offset-based pagination (1-based, default: 1).

params.description: Type-specific params. sle: query_type is ALWAYS required. sle site-level query types (summary, impact_summary, summary_trend, histogram, threshold, impacted_*, classifier_*) ALSO require scope + scope_id + metric. sle org-level (sites_sle, org_metric): query_type + org_id only. IMPORTANT: the metric parameter has two distinct namespaces depending on query_type — site-level SLE queries use SLE metric names (e.g. coverage, capacity, roaming, time-to-connect, switch-health, gateway-health, wan-link-health); insight_metrics and sle org_metric queries use insight metric names (e.g. worst-sites-by-sle, minis-top-probes) — use get_mist_constants(insight_metrics) to discover those. insight_metrics: object_type + metric always required; additionally mac is required when object_type is client, ap, mxedge, switch, or gateway (look up the mac first via find_mist_entity or get_mist_config).

site_id.description: Site UUID (required for insight_metrics and sle site-level queries; optional filter for marvis_actions). Use get_mist_config with resource_type='sites' to discover site IDs.

start_time.description: Start of time range — epoch timestamp in seconds or relative string (e.g. '-1d', '-1w', '-2h'). Supported by troubleshoot and insight_metrics. NOTE: troubleshoot supports a maximum range of 7 days from the current time.

annotations.title: Get Authenticated User Identity & Org Memberships

description: Returns the authenticated user's identity, account metadata, and organization memberships with org_id UUIDs. Call this FIRST to discover available org_ids before using get_mist_config, search_mist_data, get_mist_insights, or get_mist_stats. The response includes a 'privileges' array where each entry contains an 'org_id' and 'scope' indicating your access level. IMPORTANT: in a multi-turn session, call this tool only once and reuse the org_id from the response in all subsequent tool calls — do not call it again on every turn.
name: get_mist_self
title: Get Authenticated User Identity & Org Memberships

description:
Retrieve current-state statistics from the Mist Cloud across organizations and sites. Each stats_type targets a distinct Mist API statistics endpoint. Stats are current-state snapshots — distinct from search_mist_data (historical event/log search) and get_mist_insights (AI analytics). Time range: start_time/end_time (epoch seconds or relative like '-1d') or duration (e.g. '1d'). Pagination: if a response has has_more=true, call again with its next_cursor. Single-item lookup: provide object_id for types marked [supports object_id].

Available stats types (each line lists its scope, time-range, object_id, and valid filter keys):
[Organization]
  - org: Organization-level summary statistics (device counts, client counts, health scores) [org_id required] [time-range]
  - sites: Statistics for all sites in the organization, or a single site when object_id is provided [org_id required] [time-range] [supports object_id]
  - org_mxedges: Statistics for MX Edge devices across the organization, or a single MX Edge when object_id (mxedge_id) is provided [org_id required] [time-range] [supports object_id]
  - org_devices: Infrastructure devices (APs, switches, gateways) across the org, connected or disconnected. Use for device inventory org-wide. [org_id required] [time-range] | filters: mac, site_id, status, type
  - org_bgp: BGP peer statistics across the organization (search envelope with cursor pagination) [org_id required] [time-range] | filters: mac, neighbor_mac, site_id, vrf_name
  - org_ospf: OSPF neighbor statistics across the organization (search envelope with cursor pagination) [org_id required] [time-range] | filters: mac, peer_ip, site_id, vrf_name
  - org_peer_paths: VPN/WAN peer-path statistics across the organization (search envelope with cursor pagination) [org_id required] [time-range] | filters: mac, site_id, type
  - org_ports: Switch and gateway port statistics across the organization (search envelope with cursor pagination). No time range. [org_id required] | filters: device_type, mac, port_id, port_mac, up
  - org_tunnels: WAN and WX tunnel statistics across the organization (search envelope with cursor pagination) [org_id required] [time-range] | filters: mac, protocol, site_id, tunnel_name, type
[Site]
  - site_mxedges: Statistics for MX Edge devices at a specific site, or a single MX Edge when object_id (mxedge_id) is provided [site_id required] [time-range] [supports object_id]
  - site_wireless_clients: Statistics for associated wireless clients at a specific site, or a single client when object_id (client MAC) is provided [site_id required] [time-range] [supports object_id]
  - site_devices: Infrastructure devices (APs, switches, gateways) at a site, connected or disconnected. Use for device inventory at a site. Pass object_id to retrieve a single device. [site_id required] [supports object_id] | filters: status, type
  - site_bgp: BGP peer statistics at a specific site (search envelope with cursor pagination) [site_id required] [time-range] | filters: mac, neighbor_mac, vrf_name
  - site_ospf: OSPF neighbor statistics at a specific site (search envelope with cursor pagination) [site_id required] [time-range] | filters: mac, peer_ip, vrf_name
  - site_ports: Switch and gateway port statistics at a specific site (search envelope with cursor pagination). No time range. [site_id required] | filters: device_type, mac, port_id, port_mac, up

Filter values (keys apply per stats_type — see the lists above):
- status: Connectivity status (all|connected|disconnected), default: all
- type: Device type (ap|switch|gateway|all), default: all
- device_type: Device type (switch|gateway|all), default: all
- up: Port link state (true|false)

duration.description: Time range duration (e.g. '1d', '1h', '10m'). Alternative to start_time/end_time. Only accepted by types with time range support.

end_time.description: End of time range — epoch timestamp in seconds or relative string (e.g. 'now', '-1h'). Only accepted by types with time range support.

filters.description: Key-value filters specific to the chosen stats_type. IMPORTANT: only the filter keys shown for that stats_type above are accepted; others error. For site_devices use object_id (device UUID), not a mac filter. Ignored for single-object responses and when object_id is provided.

limit.description: Maximum results per page. A conservative per-type default applies and a hard ceiling is enforced (higher values are clamped). Pass an explicit value to override for this call.

next_cursor.description: Cursor from a prior response's next_cursor (search-envelope types only: BGP, OSPF, ports, tunnels, peer paths). When provided, all other parameters are ignored.

object_id.description: Optional single-item identifier — UUID for most types, MAC (e.g. aabbccddeeff) for site_wireless_clients. TIP: use 'id' from find_mist_entity; site_devices has no mac filter.

org_id.description: Organization UUID (required for organization-scoped stats types). Use get_mist_self to discover available org IDs.

site_id.description: Site UUID (required for site-scoped stats types). Use get_mist_config with resource_type='sites' to discover site IDs.

start_time.description: Start of time range — epoch timestamp in seconds or relative string (e.g. '-1d', '-1w', '-2h'). Only accepted by types with time range support.

name: get_mist_stats
title: Get Statistics

description:
Search for operational data across the Mist Cloud: devices, clients, events, and alarms. Each search_type targets a different Mist API search endpoint with type-specific filters. Provide org_id always. If site_id is also provided, the request is scoped to that site where the search type supports it. Client searches (wireless_clients, wired_clients, wan_clients, nac_clients) route to the org endpoint with site_id as a query filter when site_id is provided. Time range: start_time/end_time (epoch seconds or relative like '-1d', '-1w') or duration (e.g. '1d', '1h'). Pagination: default limit 25; if a response has has_more=true, call again with its next_cursor. Optional count_only and distinct parameters return counts without transferring records (see their descriptions).

Available search types:
[discovery]
  - sites: Search for sites within the org by name, address, or country code. Prefer over get_mist_config(resource_type='sites') for large orgs. Use to resolve a site_id from a partial name or location. [org] | filters: address, country_code, name
[devices]
  - devices: Search devices (APs, switches, gateways) connected to Mist. Operational/connected-state records. Use search_type='inventory' for offline/unassigned devices or to filter by serial/firmware version. [org+site] | filters: device_type, hostname, mac, model
  - inventory: Search org device inventory by MAC, name, serial, or model. All claimed devices regardless of connection state. Use 'devices' search for connected-only + hostname filter. No 'hostname' param here — use 'text' for wildcard matching. [org] | filters: device_type, mac, model, serial, site_id, status, text, version
  - mxedges: Search Mist Edge appliances by hostname. mac filter unsupported — use hostname only. [org] | filters: hostname
[clients]
  - wireless_clients: Search for wireless clients currently connected to Mist [org] [time-range] | filters: ap, band, hostname, ip, mac, ssid
  - wired_clients: Search for wired clients connected through switches [org] [time-range] | filters: device_mac, dhcp_hostname, ip, mac, text
  - wan_clients: Search for WAN clients connected through gateways [org] [time-range] | filters: hostname, ip, mac
  - nac_clients: Search for NAC (802.1X / RADIUS) clients [org] [time-range] | filters: hostname, mac, ssid, text
  - guest_authorizations: Search for guest portal authorization entries [org+site] [time-range] | filters: ssid
  - usermacs: Search user MAC address assignments (PSK/NAC user-to-device mappings) [org] | filters: mac, name
  - client_sessions: Search for wireless client session history [org+site] [time-range] | filters: ap, band, hostname, mac, ssid
[events]
  - device_events: Search for device events (AP, switch, gateway lifecycle and state changes) [org+site] [time-range] | filters: event_type, mac, text
  - wireless_client_events: Search for wireless client events (association, roaming, authentication) [org+site] [time-range] | filters: event_type, mac, ssid
  - wan_client_events: Search for WAN client events [org+site] [time-range] | filters: event_type, mac
  - nac_client_events: Search for NAC client events (802.1X authentication, RADIUS events) [org+site] [time-range] | filters: auth_type, event_type, mac, nacrule_id, nas_vendor, port_type, ssid, text, vlan
  - mxedge_events: Search for Mist Edge appliance events [org+site] [time-range] | filters: event_type, mac
  - rogue_events: Search for rogue AP detection events (site scope only) [site only] [time-range] | filters: event_type, mac, ssid
[alarms]
  - alarms: Search for org alarms (infrastructure, Marvis AI, security). Marvis types: bad_cable, dns_failure, dhcp_failure, missing_vlan, port_flap. [org] [time-range] | filters: alarm_type, group, severity

count_only.description: When true, returns only the total count of matching items without fetching any result records. Uses limit=0 on the Mist API — the minimum-cost call (zero records transferred). Response shape: {search_type, total, start_epoch, end_epoch}. Ignored when 'distinct' is also provided — distinct implies count mode.

distinct.description:
Field name to group counts by, using the Mist API /count endpoint. Returns a count breakdown per distinct value of the field — e.g. distinct='nacrule_id' returns how many events matched each NAC rule. Implies count_only behavior: no result records are returned. Items absent from 'groups' had zero events in the time window. Response shape: {search_type, distinct, groups: [{field: value, count: N}, ...], total_groups}. Not available for all search types. Supported fields vary by search_type:
Valid distinct fields by search_type:
  sites: id
  devices: site_id, mac, model
  wireless_clients: ssid, ap, site_id, band, hostname
  wired_clients: mac, site_id, ip, vlan
  wan_clients: mac, hostname
  nac_clients: type, mac, auth_type
  device_events: type, mac, site_id, model
  wireless_client_events: type, ap, ssid, site_id
  wan_client_events: type, hostname
  nac_client_events: nacrule_id, type, auth_type, port_type, nas_vendor, vlan, mac, username, ssid, site_id
  mxedge_events: type, mxedge_id
  rogue_events: type, bssid, ssid
  inventory: site_id, type, model
  mxedges: site_id, model
  usermacs: mac
  alarms: type, severity, site_id, group
  client_sessions: mac, ssid, ap, site_id, band

duration.description: Time range duration (e.g. '1d', '1h', '10m'). Alternative to start_time/end_time. Supported by event, client, and alarm search types.

end_time.description: End of time range — epoch timestamp in seconds or relative string (e.g. 'now', '-1h'). Supported by event, client, and alarm search types.

filters.description:
Valid filter keys by search_type (unsupported keys produce a helpful error):
  sites: address (Site address string (supports partial match)); country_code (Two-letter ISO country code (e.g. US, GB, DE)); name (Site name prefix to search by. A trailing wildcard (*) is added automatically — pass the plain prefix (e.g. 'HQ' matches 'HQ-London', 'HQ-Paris').)
  devices: device_type (Device type (ap|switch|gateway|router)); hostname (Hostname to filter by. Wildcard matching is applied automatically — pass a plain value (e.g. 'everest' matches 'everest', 'everest-4', 'ap-everest'). You may also supply an explicit wildcard pattern such as 'everest*' or '*campus*'.); mac (MAC address to filter by); model (Device model to filter by)
  wireless_clients: ap (MAC of the AP the client is connected to (format: aabbccddeeff, no separators)); band (802.11 radio band (24|5|6)); hostname (Hostname to filter by. Wildcard matching is applied automatically — pass a plain value (e.g. 'everest' matches 'everest', 'everest-4', 'ap-everest'). You may also supply an explicit wildcard pattern such as 'everest*' or '*campus*'.); ip (IP address to filter by); mac (MAC address to filter by); ssid (SSID to filter by)
  wired_clients: device_mac (MAC of the device the client is connected to); dhcp_hostname (DHCP-reported hostname to filter by. Wildcard matching is applied automatically — pass a plain value (e.g. "iDRAC" matches "iDRAC-DNR-LD"). Searches the dhcp_hostname field specifically, as opposed to "text" which also matches MAC.); ip (IP address to filter by); mac (MAC address to filter by); text (Prefix search on hostname or MAC address. Native matching — no wildcards needed. "iDRAC" matches "iDRAC-DNR-LD"; "70b5e8" matches by MAC prefix.)
  wan_clients: hostname (Hostname to filter by. Wildcard matching is applied automatically — pass a plain value (e.g. 'everest' matches 'everest', 'everest-4', 'ap-everest'). You may also supply an explicit wildcard pattern such as 'everest*' or '*campus*'.); ip (IP address to filter by); mac (MAC address to filter by)
  nac_clients: hostname (Hostname to filter by. Wildcard matching is applied automatically — pass a plain value (e.g. 'everest' matches 'everest', 'everest-4', 'ap-everest'). You may also supply an explicit wildcard pattern such as 'everest*' or '*campus*'.); mac (MAC address to filter by); ssid (SSID to filter by); text (Wildcard search across NAC client identity fields (username, certificate CN, and other identity attributes))
  guest_authorizations: ssid (SSID to filter by)
  device_events: event_type (Event type string) → get_mist_constants('device_events'); mac (MAC address to filter by); text (Free-text search across multiple fields (exact fields depend on search type))
